meaning: Somniosus, see genus; microcephalus, Greek mikrós “small” + kephalḗ “head”, allusion not explained, perhaps referring to its short, rounded snout compared with other sharks then included in the catch-all genus Squalus
description: A huge, thick-bodied, sluggish shark of the cold North Atlantic and Arctic, grey to blackish-brown with a short rounded snout, small eyes and small dorsal and pectoral fins; the dorsals have no spines. It swims very slowly and eats fish, seals and carrion.
depth: Surface to about 1,200 m; nearer the surface in winter
eats: Fish, skates, squid, seals and carrion
